==Problem 13==
Jamal has a drawer containing <imath>6</imath> green socks, <imath>18</imath> purple socks, and <imath>12</imath> orange socks. After adding more purple socks, Jamal noticed that there is now a <imath>60\%</imath> chance that a sock randomly selected from the drawer is purple. How many purple socks did Jamal add?

<imath>\textbf{(A) }6 \qquad \textbf{(B) }9 \qquad \textbf{(C) }12 \qquad \textbf{(D) }18 \qquad \textbf{(E) }24</imath>

==Solution 1==
After Jamal adds <imath>x</imath> purple socks, he has <imath>(18+x)</imath> purple socks and <imath>6+18+12+x=(36+x)</imath> total socks. This means the probability of drawing a purple sock is <imath>\frac{18+x}{36+x}</imath>, so we obtain <cmath>\frac{18+x}{36+x}=\frac{3}{5}</cmath> Since <imath>\frac{18+9}{36+9}=\frac{27}{45}=\frac{3}{5}</imath>, the answer is <imath>\boxed{\textbf{(B) }9}</imath>.

==Solution 2 (variant of Solution 1)==
As in Solution 1, we have the equation <imath>\frac{18+x}{36+x}=\frac{3}{5}</imath>. Cross-multiplying yields <imath>90+5x=108+3x \Rightarrow 2x=18 \Rightarrow x=9</imath>. Thus, Jamal added <imath>\boxed{\textbf{(B) }9}</imath> purple socks.

==Solution 3 very fast==
The answer is <imath>9</imath>

==Solution 4 (Testing Answer Choices) ==


The probability that a randomly selected sock is purple is: The # of purple socks ÷ The total # of socks. We can test the answer choices until we find the correct answer.


[A] If Jamal adds 6 purple socks, he will have 18 + 6 = 24 purple socks. The probability of a randomly selected sock being purple after adding 6 socks is <imath>\frac{24}{6+24+12}=\frac{24}{42}=\frac{4}{7}</imath>, which isn't equal to <imath>\frac{3}{5}</imath>. 


[B] If Jamal adds 9 purple socks, he will have 18 + 9 = 27 purple socks. The probability of a randomly selected sock being purple after adding 9 socks is <imath>\frac{27}{6+27+12}=\frac{27}{45}=\frac{3}{5}</imath>, which is indeed equal to <imath>\frac{3}{5}</imath>.


So our final answer is <imath>\boxed{\textbf{(B) }9}</imath> purple socks.
